section.sectionSummaryBrief: Based on this, the saying of the Rebbe about Pesach Sheni relating to the second soul is explained, as its leap surpasses that of Pesach Rishon by revealing the soul's essential G-dly nature.
section.t: And based on this, the saying of my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, will also be understood,
that Pesach Sheni relates to the second soul,
for the advantage of the leap of Pesach Sheni over the leap of Pesach Rishon is,
that the leap of Pesach Rishon is from the side of the concealment and hiding of the Nefesh HaBahamis
(the first soul),
and the leap of Pesach Sheni is that the "blah" (the 33) of the second soul is revealed, which is a part of Elokah from above literally.
That even when it is clothed in the body,
it is a part of Elokah from above literally, from the term "touch."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: It may be added that the leap of Pesach Sheni is incomparably greater than that of Pesach Rishon, relating to the future redemption as light of the sun versus a candle, revealing the level of Z'eir Anpin.
section.t: And perhaps one may add,
that the advantage of the leap of Pesach Sheni over the leap of Pesach Rishon is beyond comparison,
to the extent that it is a leap even relative to the leap of Pesach
(Rishon).
And analogous to what is said,
"As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders,"
that the revelations of the future redemption will be wonders even relative to the wonders that were in the Exodus from Egypt.
And the explanation of the matter
(the connection of Pesach Sheni to the future redemption)
in more detail,
is that it is stated in the Midrash,
that the redemption from Egypt
[and likewise the redemption from the Babylonian exile and the other redemptions until the future redemption]
is analogous to the light of a candle,
and the future redemption is like the light of the sun, which is not extinguished.
And it is explained in Chassidus,
that this—that the redemption from Egypt was compared to the light of a candle—
is,
that a candle is the aspect of Malchus,
and the revelation that was in the redemption from Egypt,
even though it was a revelation above the chain of descent,
was in a garment within the aspect of Malchus,
as it is written, "And Pesach (the passing over) of Hashem upon the opening,"
for "opening" is Malchus
(as above, section 1).
And from this it is understood,
that this—that the future redemption is compared to the light of the sun—is because the revelation of that which is above the chain of descent that will be then will be in the aspect of Z'eir Anpin.
And this is the connection of Pesach Sheni to the future redemption,
for the revelation of Pesach Sheni is in Yesod of Z'eir Anpin,
as above.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: May it be His will that our actions and service, especially regarding Pesach Sheni, hasten the future redemption, which will come with a greater leap, immediately and speedily.
section.t: And may it be His will,
that our deeds and our service,
and particularly in the matters related to Pesach Sheni,
will bring closer and hasten even more the future redemption,
that also the future redemption will be in a manner of a leap,
as it is stated in the Midrash,
"The voice of my Beloved... leaping upon the mountains"—this is King Moshiach,
and moreover,
in the future redemption there will be a greater leap
(analogous to
(but above)
the leap of Pesach Sheni, which is a greater leap than the leap of Pesach Rishon),
that it will not be in order and gradation from level to level at all,
as the verse states,
"Immediately they are redeemed,"
with the coming of Moshiach our righteousness,
may he come and redeem us and lead us upright to our land,
speedily in our days, literally.
